function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity wasn’t “discovered” by a single person—it emerged over centuries of observation and experimentation.  Ancient Greeks (e.g., Thales of Miletus) noted static electricity from rubbing amber, and later scholars such as William Gilbert coined the term *electricus*.  In the 18th century, Benjamin Franklin famously conducted his kite‑experiment and identified positive and negative charges.  Alessandro Volta invented the first battery (the voltaic pile), and Michael Faraday’s work on electromagnetism laid the foundations for modern electrical science.  Thus, the discovery of electricity is the cumulative achievement of many scientists rather than a single individual.
